title: Selfish Summoning
paragraphs: Three days had passed. Our journey to Faubrey was proceeding smoothly. Several times, we encountered people who suspected we were the Heroes, but we denied it and moved on.
“I-I see…”
From their demeanor, there didn’t seem to be any hostility.
“Where are you headed?”
“We are on our way to Faubrey.”
Most of them backed off without much fuss after hearing our answer. Seeing this, Father commented—
“They totally know what’s going on with us, don’t they?”
However, some were more persistent. I feel like we ran into similar types before.
“Please, come to our country instead of Faubrey!”

There were even those who actively tried to block our way. Of course, we dealt with them by paralyzing or putting them to sleep and making our escape. Their greedy ambitions were written all over their faces—it only took one move to handle them.
“It’s a bit annoying how some of them are desperately trying to get us to go to their country.”
“In that sense, the people from Siltvelt were more reasonable than expected.”

Speaking of which, a messenger from Siltvelt had approached us recently. Ah, it was a different person from the one we met while staying in Melromarc. When we told them we were heading to Faubrey, they simply stepped aside. Or rather, it seemed that Éclair had explained something to them.
“Eclair-san, what did you tell them?”
“Hmm? Ah, just that before anything else, we should hear Faubrey’s stance first. And I warned them not to think they could deceive us.”
“And they just nodded at that? How does that even work?”
“Perhaps it’s because there’s a solid justification behind it.”
“The Three Heroes Church’s ‘divine punishment’ has become famous across the world. If they get too involved, they probably fear they’ll meet the same fate.”
“I see… Motoyasu-kun’s rampage ended up working in our favor in an unexpected way.”
“Of course, there are also factions that are desperate to prove he was a false god, so we still need to be cautious.”
“Religion can sometimes prevent conflict, but it can also be the cause of it. I suppose that doesn’t change no matter what world we’re in.”

The leader of Itsuki’s faith murmured to himself. Whenever the topic turned to this, Itsuki gave off an odd aura. If we left him unchecked, things could get troublesome. Maybe it was time to give him a little lesson.
“In the end, they’re just trying to manipulate a god to suit their own convenience.”
“Exactly. But at least what Motoyasu-kun did serves as a deterrent.”
“At first, I thought it was excessive, but in the end, it removed obstacles from our journey.”
“Seriously, you never know what might work out in your favor.”
“Heroes, be careful. Don’t be too quick to nod along to sweet talk.”
“Yeah, yeah, we know.”
Father was the first to nod, and the rest of us followed. Right now, our bond was strong—we wouldn’t be fooled by shallow rhetoric.
“That’s why we say we’re heading to Faubrey. We’re following the proper course, waiting for Faubrey to officially deploy us to handle the Waves.”
Before being defeated by Father, that country truly held immense authority.

Was it the birthplace of the Legend of the Four Holy Heroes? I’m not particularly well-versed in this world’s history, but I imagine there are many different legends. In fact, I’ve seen the Filolial Legend at the sacred grounds of the Filolials. Incidentally, the Beast Spear was also found in the Filolial sanctuary.
“Yeah, we need to prioritize world peace over religious justifications.”
“Indeed. Thanks to that, the number of recruitment attempts has decreased.”
“You never know, though. Even in Japan, persistent recruiters are a thing. In another world, it might be even worse—they could still keep coming.”
The past three days had been the peak of it.
“There have been occasional attacks, but they can’t seem to keep up with Sakura and the others’ speed, so we’ve managed to handle it.”
“If they try attacking us from the air with dragons, Motoyasu-san and I can just shoot them down.”
“How many attacks have we had today?”
“Uh, three. They were all beastmen, so maybe extremists from Siltvelt?”
“I bet they’re saying stuff like ‘We can’t let them escape!’ or ‘This is a holy war!’ If Naofumi stayed put, do you think they’d stop chasing us?”
“Hey, just because Siltvelt worships the Shield Hero doesn’t mean you can just leave me behind!”
“Exactly. If Father were to stay in that country, some factions might see it as a justification to start a war.”

Previously, when Melromarc attacked, we fought back—but war is unpredictable. During the last loop, the extremists were supposedly wiped out thanks to Trash’s efforts, but their leadership still wanted to wage war. We had to rely on Father to handle negotiations properly. Even though the Three Heroes Church had faced divine punishment, remnants of its followers and Melromarc’s nobility were still around—meaning an attack was still very possible. We couldn’t afford to repeat the mistakes of the past.
“Religious matters are always a hassle.”
“Still… why has this world developed such a strong tendency to revere the Heroes as gods?”
“Now that I think about it, the people of this world completely rely on outsiders. They’ve taken dependency to an extreme.”
“From the summoned Hero’s perspective, it sounds like a dream come true. But when they’re about to lose a war, they just rely on divine intervention and summon Heroes, even if it’s their own fault.”
“Ah, it’s the classic ‘Hero vs. Demon Lord’ setup. Basically, humans and other races have been at war for ages. Since the Hero only hears one side, the Demon Lord is automatically labeled as ‘evil.’”
“I’ve seen stories like that before. Depending on the work, some even end with both sides reconciling.”
“Either way, the idea of ‘justice’ is always used as a tool for someone’s agenda.”
In response to that question, Éclair raised her hand.
“Of course, there are always those who would try such things. However, successful summonings without the use of summoning tools are extremely rare.”
“Summoning tools?”
“Also known as summoning equipment, they are the tools used to summon Heroes. Without them, the chances of calling a Hero from another world drop significantly.”
“So does having one guarantee success?”
“No.”
Éclair shook her head.
“It almost never succeeds. The Four Holy Weapons must judge it as an insignificant threat. It is said that the Four Holy Heroes are only summoned when a crisis of great magnitude arises.”
“Motoyasu-kun, do you know anything about this?”
“Unfortunately, I do not.”
“Yeah, political topics like this don’t seem worth discussing with Motoyasu-kun…”
Father muttered as if he’d come to some understanding.
“So, does that mean the summoning of the Four Holy Heroes this time was an incredibly rare occurrence?”
“There must have been some level of certainty. After all, the threat of the Waves was approaching.”
Éclair continued speaking. Come to think of it, she had gone to the guild in a town we stopped by earlier.
Could she read Siltvelt’s script?
“The fact that all four Holy Heroes were summoned together is proof that an immense threat is looming. The king and the Three Heroes Church clearly failed to recognize this reality.”
“They prioritized their own faith and desires over the world’s survival. Corruption at its peak.”
“They underestimated the phenomenon of the Waves. To them, we were just convenient pawns.”
That assessment was more or less accurate. In the first world, I—along with the others—had been treated exactly like that.
“Back to the topic—so is it more common for only one of the Four Holy Heroes to be summoned at a time?”
“Yes. I haven’t seen it myself, but most of the Holy Heroes in the past were summoned alone.”
“That means the level of threat determines the number of Heroes summoned. In those cases, a single Hero would have been enough to handle the situation, right?”
“What did the Four Holy Heroes before us accomplish?”
“From what I know… the most recent summoning was about a century ago.”
“Huh… what happened back then?”
“It was a chaotic era, and much of the records were lost. But it is said that an evil entity known as the Demon King manipulated people, attempting to take control of the world.”
“Wow, that sounds just like a classic isekai RPG!”
“In the end, the Demon King was defeated thanks to the Hero’s efforts.”
“In a way, that era might have been easier to understand—everything was black and white.”
Hmm? Something about that sounds vaguely familiar… or maybe not.
“In the future, the remnants of the Three Heroes Church caused an incident using a weapon called the ‘Leader’s Dagger,’ which could manipulate those it wounded.”
“What?”

I didn’t know the full details, but Lady Filo had discussed the incident. Of course, some Filolials had been manipulated as well. I ended up racing through the streets of Melromarc’s capital to assist Father.
“A revival of the legend?”
“Apparently, the dagger was created using a Hero’s weapon that had the ability to instill their personal beliefs into others. It even had an infectious effect.”
“There are similar stories in old legends. How was the situation resolved?”
I suppose I should start with the conclusion.
“The culprit was Itsuki, who had been deceived by the Three Heroes Church and went on a misguided crusade for justice.”
